name: Douala International Airport
before:
Cameroon's busiest airport, in Douala, the country's largest city. It handles an average of 1.5 million passengers and 50,000 tonnes of freight a year across four terminals.

There is a single runway of 2,880 metres, and that is the constraint to be aware of. When it closed for three weeks of upgrade work in March 2016, every airline had to move operations to Yaoundé, so there is no fallback on site.

That work was the first stage of a 20 billion CFA renovation financed by the French Agency of Development, with the terminals and interiors to follow.

The airport is managed and 34 per cent owned by Aeroport du Cameroon, which runs all thirteen of the country's other airports as well.
after:
Douala's international airport, about 8 km from the city centre, run by Aéroports du Cameroun (ADC).

There is a single runway of about 2,850 metres. When it closed for resurfacing from 1 to 21 March 2016, airlines moved their Douala flights to Yaoundé.

The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Cameroon, including the North-West and South-West regions, so check its advice for any onward journey.

claims.claim: busiest airport; largest city; 1.5 million passengers and 50,000 t freight; four terminals
claims.wasBefore: Cameroon's busiest airport, in Douala, the country's largest city. It handles an average of 1.5 million passengers and 50,000 tonnes of freight a year across four terminals.
claims.why: Wrong: 1.5 million passengers and 50,000 tonnes are the operator's CAPACITY ('Capacité d'accueil'), and it says 31 per cent of that is used; Wikipedia read them as traffic. The ranking, the largest-city claim and the four terminals rest on Wikipedia alone.

claims.wasBefore: There is a single runway of 2,880 metres, and that is the constraint to be aware of.
claims.why: Length corrected to about 2,850 m; 'the constraint to be aware of' is kept only as the 2016 fact that follows.

claims.claim: closed three weeks in March 2016; no fallback on site
claims.wasBefore: When it closed for three weeks of upgrade work in March 2016, every airline had to move operations to Yaoundé, so there is no fallback on site.
claims.why: Reworded to what both sources say; 'no fallback on site' was an inference.

claims.claim: first stage of a 20 billion CFA renovation by the French development agency
claims.wasBefore: That work was the first stage of a 20 billion CFA renovation financed by the French Agency of Development, with the terminals and interiors to follow.
claims.why: Only Wikipedia, and ten years old with no word on the second stage.

claims.claim: managed and 34 per cent owned by ADC, which runs all 13 other airports
claims.wasBefore: The airport is managed and 34 per cent owned by Aeroport du Cameroon, which runs all thirteen of the country's other airports as well.
claims.why: ADC as operator is kept. The 34 per cent has only Wikipedia, and the thirteen airports is contradicted by ADC itself, which lists seven airports in its concession.

opinion.text: so check its advice for any onward journey.
opinion.why: Advice attached to the attributed FCDO statement.
